title: initiative-heartbeat-and-proactive-sli-guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an 'initiative heartbeat' mechanism and proactive SLI guardrails that provide early-warning signals for SLI drift at the initiative and project level, and automatically surface shortlists of candidate mitigation actions for on-call/product owners.

Background: Our current initiative tracking shows SLI attainment only after burn is materialized into error budgets. Teams report late detections and high coordination overhead when trying to triage SLI regressions across multiple services and model routes. This ticket scopes a product-led feature that: (1) synthesizes upstream SLIs into an initiative-level health heartbeat, (2) computes short-term trajectory risk (72h/7d), and (3) exposes recommended mitigations (feature throttles, canary pause, fallback model route).

Goals: 
- Detect SLI drift with >= 48h lead time for medium-impact degradations and >= 24h lead time for high-impact degradations.
- Provide a single initiative-level health signal (green/amber/red) plus a ranked list of mitigation playbooks.
- Integrate with incident channels (Slack/Email) and the Console rollout controls to allow one-click canary pauses or fallback routing.
- Reduce time-to-mitigation for SLI regressions by 30% in the first quarter after launch.

Out-of-scope: automated rollback of customer code, engineering-only remediation workflows, changes to underlying KV cache runtime optimizations (those are separate eng tickets).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Initiative dashboard shows heartbeat with current SLI attainment, 72h trajectory, and historical trend; visible to PM/Eng/Oncall roles.
2) System computes risk band with deterministic thresholds and includes confidence band metadata.
3) For any initiative flagged amber or red, Console surfaces a ranked playbook of 3 mitigations with links to runbooks and an option to trigger an approved action (canary pause or switch to fallback variant).
4) Notifications sent to oncall rotation when risk crosses high threshold; optional suppression window configurable per initiative.
5) Instrumentation: events emitted to observability pipeline (tags: initiative_id, model_route, slo_name, risk_level) and available in trace logs.

Proposed approach: 
- Data: aggregate SLI time-series from telemetry pipeline for initiative-scoped services and model routes. Compute short-term trend via EWMA and linear-extrapolation ensemble; include simple seasonality adjustment for hourly traffic patterns.
- Risk scoring: combine current attainment gap, burn rate slope, and recent error budget consumption into a 0-100 risk score mapped into green/amber/red bands. Use guardrail thresholds that are configurable per initiative.
- Playbook generation: map risk patterns to a curated library of mitigations maintained by PMs/ResOps (throttle, downgrade quantization, switch to cheaper model variant, increase batching window). Each mitigation includes estimated cost impact and rollback steps.
- UI: new 'Initiative Heartbeat' card on Reliability Initiative Hub with summary, timeline, and action buttons.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal alpha, 2 weeks): pipe initiative heartbeat for three pilot initiatives, validate signals against historical incidents (backtest).
- Phase 2 (beta, 4 weeks): expose to all reliability leads and two customer-facing PMs; enable notifications and manual action buttons for approved playbooks.
- Phase 3 (GA, 6 weeks): open to org, tune thresholds, document runbooks, measure time-to-mitigation impact.

Metrics to track: 
- True positive lead time (hours) for detected regressions vs incident start.
- False positive rate (alerts not leading to any degradations).
- Time-to-mitigation from alert to action.
- Fraction of initiatives using configurable suppressions/playbooks.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Noise/false alarms: mitigate by backtesting on historical data and exposing confidence band; gradually loosen thresholds.
- Over-automation risk: require explicit approvals for any action that affects customer traffic; default to manual trigger for first 12 weeks.
- Data gaps: dependency on telemetry completeness; implement graceful degradation where heartbeat shows 'insufficient data'.

comments: 2026-02-22 Marco Li: Spike started. Early results show EWMA has lower false positives than plain slope for short bursts. Need to evaluate hourly seasonality removal.

2026-03-01 Rowan Kim: Initial mockups for the heartbeat card posted. UX review suggests we emphasize confidence band and recommended playbooks to reduce panic-driven actions.
2026-03-05 Diego Morales: Playbook draft attached; recommended default is manual trigger for canary pause. Also flagged requirement for audit logging on actions.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Backtest completed for three pilots. Lead-time averaged 36h for medium regressions, false positive rate ~14%. Plan: tweak thresholds and roll to beta next week.
2026-03-12 Marco Li: Implemented prototype endpoint for risk scores. Exposed feature flag 'initiative-heartbeat' in staging. Console PR opened (WIP).
